clue.text: Take risks to get chilled fish?

definitions.meaning: to court danger, as on a frozen pond that may crack beneath you
read literally, a flatfish of that name laid out on a fishmonger's bed of ice

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: the skate is the fish, and the frozen bed it lies on is the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something dangerous, as skating on fragile ice risks a plunge.

clue.text: Place in band for trumpet

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is set within the word for a band

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist
PL is the standard abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone finding a spot in a brass band for a trumpet player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpet' looks like the instrument, but it is a verb: to publicise loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash news is to display it prominently, just as to trumpet it is to proclaim it loudly.

clue.text: Wrong when on salver

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so the first word comes above the second

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left, it rained'
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: Something going wrong once it has been placed on a silver serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means going wrong or off course, so the adverb matches 'wrong' as in 'it went wrong'.

clue.text: It's seen wandering round a tree, says the Observer

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the tree
the letters of it's seen wander from their places into a new order

parts.note: the yew is a common evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A newspaper (the Observer) reports something seen roaming round a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper, but it simply means a person who observes something.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness who saw an event at first hand is literally an observer of it.

clue.text: Unacceptable, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the letters read the same forwards and backwards, so either direction of reading gives the same entry

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone declaring a thing unacceptable from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase means not acceptable or out of order, as in 'that behaviour is not on'.

clue.text: See 1
Do a letter correctly and it will be accepted

indicators.note: the letters of these three words must be put in the right order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Advice that writing a letter properly will ensure it is well received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correctly' tells you to put DOALETTER into its correct order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerated has been put up with or allowed, so it has been accepted.

clue.text: Russian bed without a head

indicators.note: the bed's word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a divan is a low bed or couch

explanation.surface: A Russian sleeping on a bed that has no headboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name, so stands for a Russian.

clue.text: I'm starting, so I'll have sago with tumbleweed

parts.note: the clue's I, with the rest of 'I'll have' only joining it to the next part

indicators.note: the slang word for a weed turns head over heels, reading backwards

parts.note: weed is slang for tobacco, and a cig is a cigarette

explanation.surface: A rambling invitation to dine on sago pudding with tumbleweed blowing past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbleweed' looks like one plant, but it splits in two: 'tumble' signals the reversal and 'weed' is the slang word turned. The answer is a rare word meaning introductory.
explanation.definitionFit: Isagogic means introductory, the words of someone who is just beginning, as in 'I'm starting'.

clue.text: Ability to see very well inside the boat

indicators.note: the agreement word goes within the word for the boat

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat rowed by eight oarsmen
very well is a way of saying yes, agreeing to something

explanation.surface: Someone with excellent vision sitting in a rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing boat crewed by eight, as in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, literally the ability to see.

clue.text: Agile and casual, but not to begin with

indicators.note: the word for casual drops its opening letter

parts.note: blithe means carefree or casually indifferent

explanation.surface: Someone nimble and relaxed, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and flexible, a close synonym of agile.

clue.text: Reveal something involving a girl in non-alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the two-letter abbreviation

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, so non-alcoholic
Ella is a girl's name
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A girl at a bar with a soft drink gives away a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'non-alcoholic' with 'drink', but the abbreviation for teetotal holds the girl and the beer comes after: ironically the drink is alcoholic.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a tale is to reveal a secret, as a telltale does.

clue.text: Euston, for example, is joined to a railway still

parts.note: Euston is a major London railway station

explanation.surface: A London terminus described as joined to a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb, but it is the adjective: not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means not moving, the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: A Hindu bear?

definitions.meaning: an ascetic Hindu who practises yoga
the cartoon bear of Jellystone Park, famous for stealing picnic baskets

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a Hindu yoga master and is also the name of a well-known cartoon bear.

clue.text: Incentive to get cover for the tea table

parts.note: a carrot is an inducement, as in carrot and stick
to cake is to coat or cover thickly, as boots caked in mud

explanation.surface: An inducement to lay a cloth on the tea table.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot cake is a classic item served with afternoon tea.

clue.text: I harm things terribly — it's like a bad dream

indicators.note: the letters are put together terribly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A confession of doing dreadful harm, likened to a nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nightmarish is frightening or horrible, as a bad dream is.

clue.text: Acts of charity performed in sizeable factory

parts.note: good can mean sizeable, as in a good number
a works is a factory or industrial plant

explanation.surface: Charitable acts carried out in a large factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Good works are charitable deeds done to help others.

clue.text: Blow the whistle to keep hands going round

indicators.note: the word for informing holds the crew within it

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, like blowing the whistle
hands are workers or sailors, together a crew

explanation.surface: A whistleblower trying to keep the clock's hands turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow the whistle' and 'sing' are both slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwing is turning, as a screw is driven round.

clue.text: Upright troops do when scattered

indicators.note: the letters of troops do are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: An upright stance that soldiers adopt when dispersed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorpost is an upright of a door frame.

clue.text: Crossworder has a change of heart about more than one country

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word swaps for another letter

explanation.surface: A crossword solver altering their feelings about foreign lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a change of heart' changes the central W of CROSSWORDER to B.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-border describes something involving or spanning more than one country.

clue.text: Before this is carried in the "Renown"

indicators.note: the entry is carried within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A remark about something once aboard the ship HMS Renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried in' signals the letters inside 'the Renown'. The Renown was a famous Royal Navy ship name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erenow is an archaic word meaning before now, before this time.

clue.text: Pad in which to make love and then rest

parts.note: to bed someone is to make love to them
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Describing a flat as a place for romance and relaxation.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British rented single room used for both living and sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is slang for a home or flat, and a bedsit is a small one.

clue.text: Unopened cyclopedia contains description of sound system

annotationWithheld.why: Unopened cyclopedia contains description of sound system (4) — no parse found: no wordplay in 'Unopened cyclopedia contains' gives EARS, and a search of the exact clue gives no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Unopened cyclopedia contains description of sound system

clue.text: 1400 hours or 1500 hours for a few

parts.note: 1400 hours is two in the afternoon
taken as written
1500 hours is three in the afternoon

explanation.surface: Two afternoon appointment times offered as alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The 24-hour times 1400 and 1500 are two o'clock and three o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Two or three is an idiom for a small number, a few.

clue.text: Type of switch, worn and disconnected

parts.note: clothes being worn are on
a device disconnected is off

explanation.surface: Describing a switch that is worn out and disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-off switch is the kind that toggles power between two states.

clue.text: Eastern place of work or play is paradise

parts.note: a den is a study for work or a playroom

explanation.surface: An eastern workplace or playground described as paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the garden of paradise in Genesis.

clue.text: So that it's possible to ride or not with a switch

indicators.note: the letters of ride or not are switched round into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that lets you choose whether to ride, using a riding crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a switch' rearranges RIDEORNOT; a switch looks like a riding crop.
explanation.definitionFit: In order to introduces a purpose, meaning so as to make something possible.

clue.text: Chaste girl degenerates about noon

indicators.note: the word for growing old goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: to age is to decline or degenerate

explanation.surface: A virtuous girl who declines in morals around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: St Agnes is the patron saint of chastity, and her name is linked to the Greek for pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a girl's name associated with chastity through St Agnes.

clue.text: Start in a new activity by walking in the rain?

definitions.meaning: to begin trying something new for the first time
read literally, what happens to your feet when you stroll in a downpour

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to gain first experience of something, as paddling first dampens your toes.

clue.text: See 27
